The University of Bern offers Digital Humanities at Master's level as a **Major (90 ECTS, four semesters)** and as a **Minor (30 ECTS, three steps)** that is combined with a Major in another subject. Both are taught at the Digital Humanities Center (Walter Benjamin Kolleg).

This page explains how the two programmes are built and in which semester each course belongs. The binding rules are in the [study plan](https://www.dh.unibe.ch/studium/studium/studienplan/index_ger.html); dates, rooms and registration are in [KSL](https://www.ksl.unibe.ch/KSL/home).

::: {.callout-tip title="Start in the autumn"}
*Introduction to Digital Humanities*, the *DH Lab* and the lecture series are taught in the **autumn semester**. The first semester of both programmes is therefore an autumn semester.
:::

**Semester overviews:** [Spring 2027](fs2027/index.qmd) · [Autumn 2027](hs2027/index.qmd)

**Questions about your study plan:** Adrian Demleitner, head of study programmes ([adrian.demleitner@unibe.ch](mailto:adrian.demleitner@unibe.ch))

## Specialisations

Major students can study broadly or choose one specialisation:

- Digital Scholarly Editing and Computational Literary Studies
- Digital Histories
- Digital Culture Studies
- Data Science
- Digital Sociolinguistics

## MA Major (90 ECTS)

| Semester | Block | Courses | ECTS |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1st** (autumn) | **Introduction** · 13 ECTS | [Introduction to Digital Humanities](https://dhbern.github.io/introduction-to-dh/) | 3 |
| | | [DH Lab](https://dhbern.github.io/dh-lab/) | 4 |
| | | [Introduction to programming](https://www.digitale-nachhaltigkeit.unibe.ch/studium/grundkurs_programmieren/index_ger.html) (Grundkurs Programmieren) | 3 |
| | | [Lecture series: Insights into the Digital Humanities](https://dhbern.github.io/dh-lecture-series/) | 3 |
| **2nd** (spring) | **Advanced studies** · 25 ECTS | Two elective seminars (6 + 6) | 12 |
| | | Colloquium: Critical Algorithm Studies | 3 |
| | | Seminar: philosophy of science / media theory | 7 |
| | | [Lecture: Introduction to DH approaches](/content/intro-lecture/index.qmd) (online, spring) | 3 |
| **3rd** (autumn) | **Application** · 22 ECTS | Elective seminar | 6 |
| | | Networking meeting and learning agreement | 1 |
| | | Project management | 3 |
| | | Presentation, Preservation, Publication (PPP) | 3 |
| | | Applied working (at least four weeks, with report) | 9 |
| **4th** (spring) | **Final phase** · 30 ECTS | Master's thesis and defence | 30 |

**Seminars and colloquia:** seminars are always worth 6 ECTS, colloquia 3 ECTS. **Elective seminars:** three seminars of 6 ECTS each, two in the 2nd and one in the 3rd semester, within or outside the specialisation. Courses with a digital focus from other programmes count after agreement with the study programme management.

### Application: from networking to thesis

The Application module (16 ECTS without the elective seminar) is practical work at an institution or in a project of the student's choice.

1. **Networking** – on the first Tuesday of the spring semester, institutions present their projects.
2. **Contract** – students contact an institution of their choice; topic and contract are checked with the thesis advisor (learning agreement, 1 ECTS).
3. **Applied working** – at least four weeks, followed by a report for the thesis advisor (9 ECTS).

The data collected or the method used may become the foundation of the Master's thesis. Partners have included the City of Zurich, the City of Bern, the Staatsarchiv Bern, the Bernisches Historisches Museum, Schloss Kyburg and the PTT-Archiv.

::: {.callout-warning title="Work in progress"}
The PPP and Project Management programmes are being revised.
:::

**Project management** consists of five short workshops and a project plan; **PPP** of six half-day mini-modules (0.5 ECTS each), run with the University Library and the Data Science Lab. Both are described in the [ILIAS course «Applied Digital Humanities»](https://ilias.unibe.ch/go/crs/3440360).

### Final phase: thesis lab

In the semester of the thesis, students report in the final-year meetings: a **project report in week 3**, a **status report in week 8**, and a **test run of the final presentation in the last week**. The thesis is concluded with a defence.

## MA Minor (30 ECTS)

| Step | Block | Courses | ECTS |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1st semester** (autumn) | **Introduction** · 13 ECTS | [Introduction to Digital Humanities](https://dhbern.github.io/introduction-to-dh/) | 3 |
| | | [DH Lab](https://dhbern.github.io/dh-lab/) | 4 |
| | | [Introduction to programming](https://www.digitale-nachhaltigkeit.unibe.ch/studium/grundkurs_programmieren/index_ger.html) (Grundkurs Programmieren) | 3 |
| | | [Lecture series: Insights into the Digital Humanities](https://dhbern.github.io/dh-lecture-series/) | 3 |
| **2nd semester** (spring) | **Advanced studies** · 9 ECTS | Elective seminar (within or outside the specialisation) | 6 |
| | | Colloquium: Critical Algorithm Studies | 3 |
| **3rd semester** (autumn) | **Final phase** · 8 ECTS | Final project | 7 |
| | | Presentation (in the final-year presentations) | 1 |

Major and Minor students attend the same courses. The final project ideally links up with the Master's thesis in the Major subject; it is reported on in the final-year meetings and presented at the end of the semester.
